For a man who possessed an impish, joyful persona, Archbishop Desmond Tutu brought nerves of steel and a fierce intelligence to his fight against Apartheid in South Africa and beating a path to national reconciliation. Pollard’s engaging film gives primacy to Tutu’s political life, but smartly orientates this within a fulsome portrait of a man whose unshakeable belief in humanity continues to inspire long after his passing.
Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, racism, and racist violence.

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.
If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.
